title: Design Agent Output — Test Plan
description: The only thing the Design Agent produces. Code Agent consumes this shape, not prose, and owns all file writing — Design Agent plans, it does not write test files. Every requirement from the source requirements.json must appear in some scenario's coversREQ or in outOfScope; every scenario's artifacts[] must resolve to an entry in the plan-wide reuse[]/newArtifacts[] pool; if scenarios.length exceeds NFR-001's typical-story threshold (6), performanceNote must be present. The validator (not just this schema) enforces all three, since JSON Schema alone can't check cross-references or conditional requirements like these.

requirementsFile.description: Path (relative to repo root) to the <TICKET>.requirements.json this plan was built from, e.g. agent-output/ResearchAgent-Output/CAP-19.requirements.json.

scenarios.description: One per test scenario. Not 1:1 with ACs — one AC may need multiple scenarios (happy-path + negative), or several related ACs may collapse into one scenario. The coversAC/coversREQ/coversEC arrays are what actually records the mapping.

title.description: Gherkin scenario name, in business language — this is what a stakeholder reads, not a technical description.

tags.description: e.g. ["@dashboard"]. Every scenario must be taggable to run alone.

steps.description: Given/When/Then outline in plain text — this is a scenario outline for Code Agent to turn into Gherkin + step definitions, not code itself.

coversAC.description: acceptanceCriteria IDs from the baseline this scenario addresses. May be empty if this scenario only covers requirements/edge cases with no direct AC.

coversREQ.description: requirements IDs from the baseline this scenario verifies. Every REQ in the baseline must show up here in some scenario, or in outOfScope — never neither.

coversEC.description: edgeCases IDs from the baseline this scenario exercises. May be empty — not every scenario needs to be edge-case-driven — but edge cases are first-class: each EC in the baseline should land in some scenario's coversEC or in outOfScope with a reason, not be silently dropped.

artifacts.description: Repo-relative paths this scenario depends on — each one MUST match a path appearing in this plan's top-level reuse[] or newArtifacts[] (enforced by the validator, not just this schema). This is how 'every scenario is implementable from reuse+newArtifacts combined' gets checked mechanically instead of just asserted in prose. Rarely empty — almost every scenario touches at least a page object.

isolation.description: parallel-safe: this scenario relies on nothing beyond Playwright's default per-test browser context (fresh localStorage, no shared storageState/persistent context) — the normal case. serial-required: this scenario depends on some resource NOT isolated by a fresh browser context (e.g. a real shared backend, a file the test suite writes outside the browser, execution order relative to another specific scenario) and must not run concurrently with whatever it conflicts with — name the conflict in isolationNotes.

isolationNotes.description: Required even for parallel-safe scenarios — state the isolation basis explicitly rather than leaving it to an unstated Playwright default (e.g. 'seeds custom state via page.addInitScript scoped to this test's own browser context; no shared storageState is used'). For serial-required, explain what it conflicts with and why.

reuse.description: Existing artifacts in THIS repo that Code Agent should reuse rather than recreate, for the plan as a whole (not per-scenario — see each scenario's artifacts[] for which of these it needs). Empty array is a valid and honest answer when nothing applies — do not invent reuse. The suite is small (2 features, 4 page objects, 2 step files); expect this to sometimes be genuinely thin.

why.description: What it provides that this plan needs — not just that it exists.

newArtifacts.description: What Code Agent must write to for this plan to be implementable, for the plan as a whole. Includes anything assumptions[] implies is needed (e.g. a seed-data fixture for edge cases the default seed data can't reach) — that need must show up here, not just in assumption prose. This covers both brand-new files (mode: create) and existing files that must gain new content (mode: extend) — never leave that ambiguous to prose alone.

path.description: Repo-relative path, following existing conventions, e.g. pages/DashboardPage.ts.

mode.description: create: path does not exist yet, Code Agent writes it from scratch. extend: path already exists (verify with Glob/Read before writing this entry) and must gain new content WITHOUT discarding what's already there — e.g. features/login.feature already has 3 scenarios; a plan adding 10 more must set mode: extend, not create, or Code Agent has no structured signal against overwriting the existing 3.

locators.description: Optional. Locator hints Design Agent observed while reading the actual bank-app source for this artifact (only meaningful for kind: page-object) — recorded so Code Agent doesn't have to re-derive from scratch what Design Agent already found. These are HINTS, not commitments: Code Agent still owns the final page object and may choose a different selector if the hint proves unreliable in practice.

element.description: What this locates, in plain language, e.g. 'Credit utilization meter'.

selector.description: The observed selector strategy, e.g. "getByRole('meter', { name: 'Credit utilization' })" — Playwright locator syntax or a plain description of the role/aria-label/text found in source.

assumptions.description: Required, may be empty. Every non-blocking ambiguity from the baseline that Design Agent proceeded past goes here, plus any new assumptions Design Agent itself had to make. These must not silently vanish — Coverage Agent surfaces them at the end. If a human answers file resolved an ambiguity, that ambiguity does NOT need an entry here (it's resolved, not assumed).

sourceAmbiguityId.description: The baseline ambiguities[].id this traces back to, if any. Null if this is a new assumption Design Agent introduced itself (e.g. about locator stability, test data, or something the baseline never raised).

text.description: What was assumed and why — plain enough for Coverage Agent to surface to a human without re-deriving context.

outOfScope.description: Requirements or ACs deliberately not covered by any scenario, with reasons. Every AC marked testable: false in the baseline belongs here, as does anything else deliberately excluded.

performanceNote.description: Required only when scenarios.length exceeds NFR-001's typical-story threshold of 6 scenarios (validator enforces this, not this schema — an optional field can't be conditionally required in a plain schema). NFR-001 defines a tiered pipeline-runtime target: <=15 minutes for a typical story (<=6 scenarios), <=25 minute ceiling for a complex story (7+ scenarios, multi-page flows). If this plan's scenario count crosses that line, say so explicitly here and state the decision: accept the longer run, or recommend splitting the ticket — don't let a plan silently blow the ceiling with no one having decided that's acceptable.
